subject: Realtime streaming lag — edge hotspot mitigation & short-term playbook
messages:
From: FastBank Ops <ops@fastbank.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 08:12:14 +0000
Subject: Realtime stream lagging (~8-12s token delays)

Hi Priya,

We're seeing a sharp increase in latency on streaming responses from the Redwood API starting ~07:55 UTC. Our users report long pauses between chunks (8-12s) and some sessions time out for long conversations. This is affecting our in-product support chat and a small portion of our production users.

Quick notes:
- Region: eu-west-1 endpoints (we pinned region to eu-west).
- Sample session IDs attached in the HAR.
- This started right after a large batch of long-context conversations (many >8k tokens) began around 07:50.

Can your team confirm whether there are any incidents on your side? We can hop on a call if that helps.

Thanks,
Suzanne Ho
Sr. Ops Engineer, FastBank
ops@fastbank.com

Attachment: client-har-20270530.jsonl (14KB)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: FastBank Ops <ops@fastbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 08:25:02 +0000
Subject: Re: Realtime stream lagging (~8-12s token delays)

Hi Suzanne — thanks for the report and for the HAR. We're seeing increased tail latency in a subset of eu-edge shards and are investigating.

Immediate actions (short-term mitigation we can try now):
- If you can, temporarily reduce per-connection concurrency (client-side) to 4 concurrent streams and retry with exponential backoff (0.5s, 1s, 2s).
- For long contexts, set max_new_tokens to 512 and prefer incremental prompts (split long context into recent+summary).
- Optional: call the non-streaming generate endpoint for a short period (response_mode=sync) — this will trade throughput for fewer chunking-related stalls while we triage.

We're provisioning an operations runbook and will update you in ~30–45 minutes. Can we schedule a quick 15-min bridge at 09:15 UTC to go over traces?

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 08:41:33 +0000
Subject: RE: Realtime stream lagging (~8-12s token delays)

TL;DR: edge shard hotspot + KV-cache thrash caused by concurrent large-context sessions + metadata compaction job. Short-term: route traffic off the shard, bump cache size and disable compaction job until patch.

Details and evidence:
- We observed evictions in the KV cache on eu-edge-7 coincident with a metadata compaction cron that ran at 07:50 UTC. The compactor scans large session contexts and triggered repeated cache misses, causing backend stalls when streaming large contexts.
- Session traces show long waits on cache retrieval (see session-trace-1234.zip attached).

Immediate operational mitigations (what we can do within 10–30 minutes):
1) Re-route FastBank's traffic away from eu-edge-7 to eu-edge-2 by adding a temporary routing tag on your requests: X-REDWOOD-PREFERRED-EDGE: eu-edge-2 (we'll honor it for this customer).
2) Disable the metadata compaction job for the next 2 hours (ops already pushed the disable flag to eu-edge-7).
3) Increase KV cache size on eu-edge-7 by +25% (in progress, rolling patch).

Client-side suggestions (confirming Priya's notes):
- Reduce per-connection concurrency and lower max_new_tokens where possible.
- If switching to sync responses is acceptable for critical flows, that reduces token-chunking sensitivity.

I'll keep an active watch and post updates to the bridge.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:05:10 +0000
Subject: Re: Realtime stream lagging (~8-12s token delays) — immediate workarounds & next steps

Suzanne — quick update from the bridge at 08:55 UTC:
- We've temporarily re-routed your traffic off eu-edge-7 and disabled metadata compaction on that host. Early telemetry shows a significant reduction in chunk pause frequency for a subset of sessions.

Please apply these two quick client toggles while we stabilize:
1) Add header: X-REDWOOD-PREFERRED-EDGE: eu-edge-2 (server honors immediately)
2) If possible, set max_new_tokens=512 and limit concurrent streams per client to 3–4.

If you want us to, we can flip your account to eu-edge-2 server-side while you keep your SDK unchanged; this would be a short maintenance window (~2 minutes) and is reversible.

We will follow up within 24 hours with:
- A root-cause summary and permanent remediation plan
- An estimated SLA credit if this outage materially affected your users (we've drafted a proposal and attached it).

Would you like us to perform the server-side reroute now, or do you prefer to apply the client header yourself?

Thanks for the quick repro artifacts — that made triage much faster.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: FastBank Ops <ops@fastbank.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:40:02 +0000
Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps — FastBank streaming latency (eu-edge-7)

Suzanne / FastBank team — follow-up after yesterday's incident. Summary and next steps below. Full postmortem is live at the link included.

What happened:
- Root cause: A scheduled metadata compaction job overlapped with a sudden burst of several long-context sessions (>8k tokens) routed to eu-edge-7. The compaction work caused repeated KV cache evictions leading to higher cache miss latency and downstream backpressure in the streaming path.

Impact:
- Time window: 07:50–09:10 UTC on 2027-05-30
- Symptoms: intermittent chunk pauses of ~8–12s for ~3% of your streaming sessions; increased client retries and early-term session closures for a small fraction of traffic.

What we did (short-term fixes applied):
- Disabled compaction cron on eu-edge-7 and re-routed FastBank to eu-edge-2 for immediate recovery.
- Increased KV cache allocation on eu-edge-7 and applied a temporary eviction-smoothing patch.
- Provided client-level mitigations (reduce concurrency, lower max_new_tokens, optional sync mode).

Permanent remediation plan (timeline):
- RINF-4512: Harden compaction job scheduling and add shard-awareness to avoid compaction during high-throughput windows (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Improve KV cache eviction heuristics and pre-warm logic (ETA: 1 week for patch, 3 weeks for rollout).
- Add per-customer temporary routing controls in Console so you can pin preferred edge without header changes (ETA: 4 weeks).

Customer compensation:
- We drafted an SLA credit proposal attached; we will finalize after you confirm the scope of affected sessions.

Next steps for FastBank:
- If you'd like help flipping to eu-edge-2 server-side now, we can schedule a 10-min maintenance.
- We'll keep RINF-4512 updated in Jira and share progress.

Apologies for the impact — we know latency in chat is user-visible and disruptive. We'll follow up with a short technical readout for your infra team next week.

Best,
Priya
